summary.name: MyPack
summary.one_liner: MyPack is a free, open-source tool that turns any website or local HTML project into a standalone desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux.
use_cases: Turn a web service into its own desktop app with a Dock icon
Package a local HTML or static site project as a desktop app
Run several sites in one window with separate sessions
Keep separate logins for different accounts on the same site
Let AI agents create and build desktop apps through an MCP server
summary.what_it_does: MyPack takes a pasted URL, a dropped HTML file, or a project folder and builds a desktop app around it, fetching the site's name and icon that you can change. It writes the app's settings into a prebuilt runtime, so no Go, Rust, Node or Xcode is needed on your machine. Each app gets its own window, icon, notifications, Dock badge, and separate sign-in, and uses the system WebView. A Library lets you install, update, repair, uninstall, sync via a shared folder, or export .mypack files. The same binary provides a CLI with JSON output and an MCP server for agents.
notable: Builds without a developer toolchain using a prebuilt runtime
Open source under Apache-2.0 with no license keys or account
Reads Pake configs and offers a CLI and MCP server for agents
Supports local projects from Vite, CRA, Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit and Next exports
caveats: Releases are not yet signed, so macOS Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen may block the first launch
Windows support is described as less tested so far
The page's comparison table is self-reported and dated November 2026
